title: The hazelnut
hookLine: Julian is shown a hazelnut: it lasts because God loves it (Revelations 5)

cards: There's a photograph of Earth taken from far out in space. A tiny blue dot, smaller than a grain of sand in a sunbeam. Everything you've ever known is on it: every person you've loved, every war, every wedding.
You could cover it with your fingertip. It can stir wonder, and a little fear. How does something that small and fragile keep going?
Centuries before any camera, a woman lying sick in Norwich was shown something like that picture. Not a planet. Something she could hold in her hand.

teach.h: A LITTLE THING IN HER PALM.
teach.b: It's in the fifth chapter of Julian's book, early in her showings. She says she was shown a little thing, about the size of a hazelnut, lying in the palm of her hand, round as a ball.
The kind of nut you'd crack at Christmas. She looked at it with what she calls the eye of her understanding, and wondered: what can this be?

teach.h: IT IS ALL THAT IS MADE.
teach.b: The answer came, in Grace Warrack's 1901 version: "It is all that is made." The whole creation. The sky and the sea and every living thing, and Julian herself, the size of a nut in her palm.
Her first reaction is close to the blue-dot feeling. She marveled that it could last at all; it seemed so small it might just fall into nothing. And the answer she was given is the heart of today.

teach.h: IT LASTS BECAUSE GOD LOVES IT.
teach.b: It lasts, and always will, because God loves it. Not because it's strong. Not because it's important.
Because it's loved. Then she sees three things in that little nut. God made it.
God loves it. God keeps it. And she draws a conclusion: we won't find rest in things that are made, because they're so small.
We rest only in the one who made them. But she doesn't despise the little nut. It's loved, after all.
Whatever feels fragile right now, a body, a marriage, a job, the whole world on the news, Julian says the same thing about it: it lasts because it's loved.

how: Some readers of Julian keep a hazelnut or a small stone as a reminder of her vision, and some prayer groups hold one in the hand while praying.

o: a sign that God is pleased with small gifts
Julian's picture of all creation in her palm
a symbol of the food Julian ate in her cell

s: Julian says the world lasts because it's strong
it lasts, and always will, because God loves it.
the hazelnut stood for all of creation
Julian says to find rest in created things
she says we rest only in the one who made them, though the little thing is loved.

games.q: you're holding all of creation in your palm. it's the size of a hazelnut. it looks like it could vanish. what's your first feeling?
o: wonder that it could last at all.
games.why: Julian marveled that it could last. the answer: it lasts, and always will, because God loves it.

practice: Hold something tiny in your palm, a nut, a bean, a pebble, a button, a ring, or cup your empty hand and imagine one. Look at it and think: this is how small everything is.
Then, if it helps, say the three things quietly, made, loved, kept, and let your hand stay open.

wordCard.voice: The hazelnut. Julian's picture of all creation, tiny in her palm, lasting because God loves it.

carryVoice: Your line: it lasts because it's loved. Small as a nut: made, loved, kept. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Julian of Norwich, Revelations of Divine Love, ch. 5
sources.q: It is all that is made.
